question.text: A constant current was passed through a solution of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msubsup><mi>AuCl</mi><mn>4</mn><mo>-</mo></msubsup></math> ion between gold electrodes. After a period of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn></math> minutes, the increase in mass of cathode was <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>314</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math>. The total charge passed through the solution is ___<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math>. (Given atomic mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Au</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>197</mn><mo>)</mo></math>

solution.text:
The half-cell reaction is,

Au3+ + 3e− → Au

Given W = 1.314 g

Atomic mass of Au=197

When one Faraday of charge is passed through a circuit, then one equivalent of charge is deposited at the respective electrode.
